state: Fixture requests in Can assertions are ordered by full lexical invocation paths and may proceed only with zero reserved/running frames. Each admission activates the chosen frame before native Promise delivery; explicit park/finish operations determine when another admission is possible. Requests can be inserted between selections at positions earlier than queued paths. All invocation identities are distinct. The production comparator is a stable total order, but conformance supplies reversed, throwing or nonfinite comparisons; a bad comparison must fail every pending request and return those frames to running. Repeated scanning, sorting and front-removal currently produces 499510 comparisons for1000 requests and7998010 for4000, a quadratic growth defect. Existing empty-aggregate selection guards must be preserved. Native Can operations remain native; the internal scheduling adapter has no Bun priority queue available. Target complexity is O(1) to establish quiescence and O(log n) to update ordering on insertion/removal. One design counts blocking phases during transitions and retains a binary minimum heap with enqueue sequence numbers to break ties, staging arrivals until the scheduler pump and tracking all pending requests in a separate set for safe comparator-error rejection. Other designs keep a sorted-array cache and re-sort on arrivals, leaving an interleaved worst case, or make no algorithmic change.

scheduler.instructions: Identify the design that preserves the required semantics while removing the repeated-work bound.

criteria.priority_heap: Track blocking-frame counts and use a stable minimum heap with staged additions and an independent pending set for failure cleanup, retaining explicit barriers and single native delivery at a time.
criteria.sorted_cache: Maintain a cached array order and invalidate it on incoming requests, then perform a fresh native sort alongside constant-time active tracking.
criteria.unchanged: Preserve the current repeated frame enumeration, queue sorting and shifting.
